text: hahahaha 512 it finllay gets choppy. at 220, no lag tho
resolution: Diagnosed the 512-block choppiness (the user's found ceiling: 507 km2 / 776k instances chops, 220 blocks / 143k is glass-smooth at 240fps). Root cause is NOT draw cost — it is the per-INSTANCE buffer g_instance_buf in framework/gpu/3d.zig drawScene being re-staged (makeInstance loop) and queue.writeBuffer RE-UPLOADED EVERY FRAME for a world that never moves: ~11MB/frame at 143k (fine), ~59MB/frame at 776k (chops). The framework already uploads VERTEX geometry once and caches it (g_retained_vbuf, 'upload that never runs again'), but the instance batch has no such static path. The fix (offered, not yet built) is a static/retained instance buffer mirroring g_retained_vbuf: upload the world's instance batch once at load, redraw each frame without restage/re-upload — the player is separate mesh nodes so the world batch is genuinely static. That removes the per-frame cost and pushes the ceiling to GPU vertex throughput (millions of instances). Saved the full caps map + choke to memory (hmsc_massive_scale_caps.md) so it is not re-derived. No code changed this turn — diagnosis only.
